precepts.text: Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees. So who burned the temple? The Edomites.
precepts.point: Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape: when we were escaping, Edom blocked our way, held us in, and gave us up to the Babylonians.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Obadiah is “concerning Edom”: the whole chapter is about Edom and what they did. “In the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.” Even Edom was as one of them. First Esdras names the deed plainly: “Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.”

So who burned the temple? The Edomites. The history agrees: when the first temple was destroyed in 586 BC, Edom aided the Babylonian Empire rather than helping Judah, their brother. They rejoiced, looted the city, blocked the survivors fleeing, and took part in razing Solomon's temple. The brother of the Israelites assisted the Babylonians, which were Cushites, in destroying the first temple.

That is every charge in Obadiah. “Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger”: the twelve tribes did become strangers. “Neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction”: they rejoiced when we got destroyed. They “laid hands on their substance”: they were robbing us too. They “stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape”: when we were escaping, Edom blocked our way, held us in, and gave us up to the Babylonians.

That is why the Psalm cries, “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” Rase it: destroy it. That is what Edom did when they burned down that temple, and it is why Edom is called the daughter of Babylon, because they assisted the Cushite Babylonians: “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”.

precepts.text: Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes. Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women. Men have died behind the woman. We had a brother whose wife was jumping out of a moving car; we told him, you are tripping, she does not believe, and he said, I cannot leave. You can be enticed by many different things if you cannot help yourself, willing to go through years of demise and despair. And vice versa: a lot of you sisters will follow after a man when we told you, sis, he is not right; he is tall, dark, and handsome, but he is a demon. We warned you. When you decide to lay down with that man and it does not go the way you want, it is not on the counsel to fix it; you made him your lord, and now the counsel cannot come in and dictate his house against the law of marriage. Our job is to use the scriptures to give wise counsel, not to change somebody's rules in their own household. Everything in America is dictated on the aspect of the woman. Men will do much evil to get attraction from women: the way they dress, the jewels, the car, the money; all of that is to entice a woman, and it is deceitful.
precepts.point: This was Zorobabel, in the contest to reason out what is the strongest thing we deal with. O ye men, it is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that excelleth; who is it then that ruleth them, or hath the lordship over them? are they not women?

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
Zorobabel, in the contest to reason out the strongest thing we deal with, says, “it is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that excelleth; who is it then that ruleth them, or hath the lordship over them? are they not women?” Then he proves it: “Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes. Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women.”

Negroes have died behind the woman; let that be clear. Negroes have died behind the box. We had a brother whose wife jumped out of a moving car. We told him, bro, you are tripping, she don't believe. And he said, it's so good, I can't leave it. You crazy; it ain't worth it; you are going to go to jail. You can be enticed by so many things, if you cannot help yourself, that you are willing to go through years of demise and despair because of the box. Many have perished, have erred, and sinned for women.

And vice versa. A lot of you sisters are sitting ducks. You follow after a man when you have been told, sis, he ain't right. He is tall, dark and handsome, and you think everything about him is good, but he is a demon. We warned you. So when you decide to lay down with that man and it does not go the way you want, it is not on the counsel to fix your marriage. That is your lord now; you did that. We cannot go against it and come in and dictate his house. Our job is not to change somebody's rules in their own household; our job is to use the scriptures to give wise counsel.

America has dictated everything on the aspect of the woman. Negroes will kill, rob and do all kinds of evil to get the attraction of women. The way they dress, the jewels, the necklace, the car, the money rolled down the arm: that is not for dudes, that is to entice a woman, and it is deceitful as hell. That is how strong the thing Zorobabel named is, and why it rules over kings and wine alike.

precepts.text: Persia decreed the Edomites give back the villages of the Jews they held; they moved in the moment we were carried away.
precepts.point: The Edomites should give over the villages of the Jews which then they held: when Babylon took us they moved into our land, until Persia put them out. It is always them trying to take our land.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
Darius had vowed “to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.” Edom was already conquered, and still it helped the Babylonians overthrow Judah; the Edomites were the ones who burned the first temple, and as the Romans they destroyed the second.

Then Darius the Persian decreed “that all the country which they hold should be free without tribute”: the Jews going up were to be free from all taxing. And “that the Edomites should give over the villages of the Jews which then they held”.

Villages they held? When we were overthrown by the Babylonians, the Edomites moved in. They burned our temple and moved into our land, because of that hatred. That land belongs to us. They destroyed us out of the land with the Babylonians and then came along and dwelt in it, and Persia said, you do not belong here, and put them out.

It is always them trying to take our land. In the days of the Moabite king in Judges, “he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and smote Israel, and possessed the city of palm trees.” Edom always had a strong desire to take our land, going right back to the blessing he lost and the birthright he gave away; he always felt he should have it all. That is them today. This is war.

precepts.text: Men let gold and silver go and fix their eyes fast on a comely woman; by this ye must know that women have dominion over you.
precepts.point: Men gather gold and silver and every goodly thing, then let all those things go and fix their eyes fast on a woman comely in favour and beauty. Many run out of their wits for a woman and become servants for their sakes; Jacob became a servant fourteen years, because he was deceived and served another seven.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

precepts.why:
Jacob served seven years for Rachel, “and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.” That is how fine she was to him: with six and a half years still left, it felt like a couple of days. Here is why.

“Yea, and if men have gathered together gold and silver, or any other goodly thing, do they not love a woman which is comely in favour and beauty?” Men gather every goodly thing, then, “letting all those things go, do they not gape, and even with open mouth fix their eyes fast on her”. And “have not all men more desire unto her than unto silver or gold, or any goodly thing whatsoever?” “A man leaveth his own father that brought him up, and his own country, and cleaveth unto his wife”, and “remembereth neither father, nor mother, nor country.”

The conclusion is plain: “By this also ye must know that women have dominion over you: do ye not labour and toil, and give and bring all to the woman?” Jacob labored and toiled seven years and gave it all for Rachel, and counted it as nothing.

precepts.text: Many have run out of their wits for women and become servants for their sakes; Jacob served fourteen years for Rachel.
precepts.point: Men gather gold and silver and every goodly thing, then let all those things go and fix their eyes fast on a woman comely in favour and beauty. Many run out of their wits for a woman and become servants for their sakes; Jacob became a servant fourteen years, because he was deceived and served another seven.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

precepts.why:
“Wherefore a man loveth his wife better than father or mother. Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes.”

Jacob is one of them. He became a servant for Rachel's sake, and not for seven years only: he was deceived and served another seven, so that he became a servant fourteen years for a woman. Seven years “seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her”; that is a man run out of his wits for a woman, exactly as the scripture says.

precepts.text: Men bear rule over sea and land, but yet the king is more mighty; this is the debate before the king of Persia over what is strongest.
precepts.point: The Most High told Samuel to go in with a heifer, as if coming only to sacrifice; he would go incognito, not letting it be known that he was coming to anoint Saul's replacement, and the Most High would show him whom to anoint.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“And Samuel said, How can I go? if Saul hear it, he will kill me.” Remember the influence and love Samuel had among the people; even so, this shows the power of the king. Saul raised no hand against Samuel yet, but a king had the authority to command a prophet’s death.

The debate before the king of Persia over what is strongest says the same: “O ye men, do not men excel in strength that bear rule over sea and land and all things in them? But yet the king is more mighty: for he is lord of all these things, and hath dominion over them; and whatsoever he commandeth them they do.”

precepts.text: The king is only one man, but if he command to kill, they kill; that is the power Saul held, and why Samuel had cause to be careful.
precepts.point: The Most High told Samuel to go in with a heifer, as if coming only to sacrifice; he would go incognito, not letting it be known that he was coming to anoint Saul's replacement, and the Most High would show him whom to anoint.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“And yet he is but one man: if he command to kill, they kill; if he command to spare, they spare”. The king is only one man, but if he command to kill, they kill. That is the power Saul held, and why Samuel had cause to be careful.

So the Most High told Samuel, “Take an heifer with thee, and say, I am come to sacrifice to the Lord.” He would go incognito, as if coming only to sacrifice, not letting it be known that he was coming to anoint Saul’s replacement, and the Most High would show him whom to anoint: “thou shalt anoint unto me him whom I name unto thee.”

precepts.text: Zerubbabel the wise guard is granted his request by the king above what he asked.
precepts.point: The first wave came led by Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, and the other chief men. Zerubbabel had been one of the bodyguards of the Persian Empire, the wisest guard granted a request in 1 Esdras.

note.label: Ezra 2: The Register of Those Who Returned

precepts.why:
Zerubbabel, who led the first wave up out of the captivity with Jeshua, Nehemiah and the other chief men, had been one of the bodyguards of the Persian Empire. In 1 Esdras he is the wisest of the guards, and the king tells him, “Ask what thou wilt more than is appointed in the writing, and we will give it thee, because thou art found wisest; and thou shalt sit next me, and shalt be called my cousin.”

That is how the children of the province came to go up: the king granted Zerubbabel his request above what he asked, and the men whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away unto Babylon “came again unto Jerusalem and Judah, every one unto his city”, with Zerubbabel at their head.

precepts.text: Zerubbabel's wisdom before the king shows that a woman holds power over even the great king, so Esther should not fear to use the influence she has.
precepts.point: So Mordecai went his way and did according to all Esther commanded him. She had her mind set right, ready to risk her life for her people.

note.label: Esther 4: Mordecai Charges Esther for Such a Time as This

precepts.why:
Esther sets her mind: “so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.” She is ready to risk her life for her people. But she is not going in with nothing; she is a woman, and a woman holds power over even the great king.

Zerubbabel proved that before the king in his wisdom: “is not the king great in his power? do not all regions fear to touch him? Yet did I see him and Apame the king’s concubine, the daughter of the admirable Bartacus, sitting at the right hand of the king, And taking the crown from the king’s head, and setting it upon her own head; she also struck the king with her left hand. And yet for all this the king gaped and gazed upon her with open mouth: if she laughed upon him, he laughed also: but if she took any displeasure at him, the king was fain to flatter, that she might be reconciled to him again.”

All regions feared to touch the king, and a woman took the crown off his head and struck him, and he flattered her to be reconciled. So Esther should not fear to use the influence she has. The law said death for coming in uncalled, but a woman's influence over the king was real, and she went in to use it for Israel.

precepts.text: Not only the Chaldeans but the Edomites took part in burning the temple when Judea was made desolate.
precepts.point: Edom were Babylon's personal cheerleaders, calling for Jerusalem and the temple to be razed to the foundation; the daughter of Babylon that Edom cheered on became the mother of harlots, Babylon the great, which is to be destroyed.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

precepts.why:
“Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.” Not only the Chaldeans but the Edomites took part in burning the temple when Judea was made desolate.

So when Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard “burned the house of the Lord, and the king’s house; and all the houses of Jerusalem”, the Chaldeans birthed this destruction, but Edom, the so-called white man, took part in it. Esau loves burning things, which is ironic since he is destined to burn forever, wasted away by the same fire he loved to waste these nations with.

points: Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes.
Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women. Many brothers have gone out of their wits for women and become servants to women.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Then the third, who had spoken of women and of the truth, this was Zerubbabel, began to speak: O ye men, it is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that excelleth; who is it then that ruleth them? are they not women? When the first said wine is the strongest, and the second said the king, they wanted brownie points; Zerubbabel cut both down. And when he said it is not women either, that is for the brothers who say the woman is the goddess of the earth, the mother goddess; that is brown nosing, and these women fall for it.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Women have borne the king and all the people that bear rule by sea and land; they nourished them up that planted the vineyards; these also make garments for men. So sisters, if you have no sewing skills, why not learn? These bring glory unto men; and without women cannot men be.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Do they not love a woman which is comely in favour and beauty? Sisters, do not let yourself fall apart; some of you get married and just let yourself go. Take care of yourselves.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: A man leaveth his own father that brought him up, and his own country, and cleaveth unto his wife. Brothers, in order to do that, what do you have to have? A job. We were talking to the young men last night: you want to get married, but you keep getting fired? Then you cannot get married.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: By this also ye must know that women have dominion over you: do ye not labour and toil, and give and bring all to the woman? A man can have a little mean cottage and be content; it is the woman that wants the three bedroom, the two bathroom, the king size bed, the drapes.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Yea, a man taketh his sword, and goeth his way to rob and to steal, to sail upon the sea and upon rivers; and looketh upon a lion; and when he hath stolen, spoiled, and robbed, he bringeth it to his love. Men rob and steal for women. Sisters, ask yourself why brothers get in the drug game: money, power, respect; and that is how they get the woman. And when the cops come, she plays innocent: I did not know he was a drug dealer. How did he get all those vehicles with no job? You knew.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Wherefore a man loveth his wife better than father or mother. Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes; many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women. What kind of man is that, brothers? Many men have died for women, erred for women, sinned for women, and a lot of them are in jail today.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Yet did I see him and Apame the king's concubine, the daughter of the admirable Bartacus, sitting at the right hand of the king, and taking the crown from the king's head, and setting it upon her own head; she also struck the king with her left hand. And yet for all this the king gaped and gazed upon her with open mouth: if she laughed upon him, he laughed also; but if she took any displeasure at him, the king was fain to flatter, that she might be reconciled to him again. O ye men, how can it be but women should be strong, seeing they do thus?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Then the king and the princes looked one upon another: they were shocked; he insulted the king; he told everybody, that woman over there smacked you and took the crown off your head. You are not supposed to talk like that, but Zerubbabel did. So he began to speak of the truth.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: O ye men, are not women strong? great is the earth, high is the heaven, swift is the sun in his course; is he not great that maketh these things? Therefore great is the truth, and stronger than all things. All the earth calleth upon the truth, and the heaven blesseth it: all works shake and tremble at it, and with it is no unrighteous thing.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Wine is wicked, the king is wicked, women are wicked, all the children of men are wicked; and there is no truth in them; in their unrighteousness also they shall perish. Now he calls the king wicked to his face. There is no truth in the king, no truth in wine, no truth in men, no truth in women.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: As for the truth, it endureth, and is always strong; it liveth and conquereth for evermore. With her there is no accepting of persons or rewards: that is why he was so bold to tell a king, you are not the strongest. He was not partial; he said, I am going to tell you like it is. She doeth the things that are just, and she is the strength, kingdom, power, and majesty, of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: And with that he held his peace, and all the people then shouted, and said, Great is Truth, and mighty above all things. Then said the king, Ask what thou wilt more than is appointed in the writing, and we will give it thee, because thou art found wisest; and thou shalt sit next me, and shalt be called my cousin.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Notice how noble our forefather was: he asked nothing for himself. He said, Remember thy vow, which thou hast vowed to build Jerusalem, and to send away all the vessels that were taken away out of Jerusalem, which Cyrus set apart when he vowed to destroy Babylon. Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees. He did not say give me silver, give me gold, give me this woman to marry; he thought about his people and the temple. That should be our mentality. That is why I said, to be of the king's guard you had to be of a special sort, and Zerubbabel was that top guy.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

No officer, no ruler, no lieutenant, nor treasurer should forcibly enter into their doors; all the country which they hold should be free without tribute, no taxes; and the Edomites should give over the villages of the Jews which then they held. Pay attention to that: after Edom burned down the temple, they took over the land, and now the decree was to give it back.

points: If he bid them make war the one against the other, they do it; if he send them out against the enemies, they go, and break down mountains, walls, and towers.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: If he command to kill, they kill; if he command to spare, they spare; if he command to build, they build; if he command to cut down, they cut down.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: He lieth down, he eateth and drinketh, and taketh his rest; and these keep watch round about him, neither may any one depart and do his own business.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: Then the third, who had spoken of women and of the truth, this was Zorobabel, began to speak: It is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that excelleth.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: Women have borne the king and all the people that bear rule by sea and land; even of them came they, and they nourished them up that planted the vineyards, from whence the wine cometh.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: A man leaveth his own father that brought him up, and his own country, and cleaveth unto his wife; and remembereth neither father, nor mother, nor country.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: The king himself, whom all regions fear to touch, sat and gazed with open mouth upon Apame the king's concubine, who took the crown from his head and set it upon her own.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: Then he began to speak of the truth: Great is the earth, high is the heaven, swift is the sun in his course; is not he great that maketh these things? therefore great is the truth, and stronger than all things.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: All the earth calleth upon the truth, and the heaven blesseth it: all works shake and tremble at it, and with it is no unrighteous thing.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: Wine is wicked, the king is wicked, women are wicked, all the children of men are wicked; and in their unrighteousness they shall perish.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: As for the truth, it endureth, and is always strong; it liveth and conquereth for evermore. With her there is no accepting of persons or rewards, but she doeth the things that are just.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: She is the strength, kingdom, power, and majesty, of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth. And all the people then shouted, and said, Great is truth, and mighty above all things.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: The king said unto him, Ask what thou wilt more than is appointed in the writing, and we will give it thee, because thou art found wisest.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: Zorobabel asked the king to remember the vow he had vowed to build Jerusalem in the day he came to his kingdom, and to send again all the vessels that were taken away out of Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: Darius stood up and kissed him, and wrote letters that he and all those that go up with him to build Jerusalem should be safely conveyed on their way, and that cedar wood should be brought from Libanus.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: He wrote for the freedom of all the Jews that went up out of his realm, that no officer nor ruler nor lieutenant should forcibly enter into their doors, and that their country should be free without tribute.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: He appointed twenty talents yearly to the building of the temple until it were built, and ten talents yearly to maintain the burnt offerings upon the altar every day, and provided for the priests' vestments and the charges of the Levites.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: When this young man was gone forth, he lifted up his face to heaven toward Jerusalem, and praised the King of heaven, saying, From thee cometh victory, from thee cometh wisdom, and thine is the glory, and I am thy servant.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: He took the letters, and went out, and came unto Babylon, and told it all his brethren.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things

points: They praised the God of their fathers, because he had given them freedom and liberty to go up and to build Jerusalem, and the temple which is called by his name; and they feasted with instruments of musick and gladness seven days.

note.label: 1 Esdras 4: Great Is the Truth, and Mighty Above All Things
